The two `.changeset/*.md` files are prose faces, judged under ② only; the lane seat's ACCEPT owns them.

Reviewed read-only against card objectui#12486 (body and every comment), its parent objectui#12464 with triage ruling `6190403616` and the unlock `6215013185`, the PR body and file list, the net diff of the head against its merge-base with `main` (`4be76e03`), and the check-runs on the head. Neither the dispatch order nor the dispatching seat's conclusions were inputs.

### ① Derived judgments

**The arm, and what the renderer now does — right.** On `main` the `PageRenderer` compiled a node's `source` when `kind` was `html` or `jsx`. At this head the one remaining compile arm is `kind === 'html'`. A raw node that still carries `kind: 'jsx'` is a kind the renderer does not name: it falls through to `resolveTemplate` and then the page-type switch (`home` / `app` / `utility` / `record`), exactly as a node with `kind: 'full'`, `kind: 'slotted'` or no `kind` does, and its `source` is never read. No alias, no `??` fallback and no named refusal arm were added in the consumer, which is the rule for an internal contract whose refusal already sits at the producer. The pin's `same path` row holds the two renders DOM-identical, so the fall-through is measured, not assumed. The `getJsxManifest` comment now names `kind:'html'`.

**Can any producer still hand it `jsx` — no, each one checked.**
- Served pages: the resolved spec at the head is `18.0.0-next.2` for every importer in `pnpm-lock.yaml` (no `18.0.0-next.1` version line remains; `packages/types` and `packages/app-shell` range `^18.0.0-next.2`, `packages/components` range `^18.0.0-next.1`, all resolving next.2). In the published next.2 dist, `PageSchema.kind` is `enumWithRetiredValues(['full', 'slotted', 'html', 'react'], PAGE_KIND_RETIRED_GUIDANCE)`: `jsx` is refused at parse with a prescription naming `html`, so the save door, `os validate` and `defineStack` refuse it before a renderer sees it. `COMPILED_PAGE_KINDS` is `['html']`.
- Stored rows: the dist's `applyConversionsToStoredItem` calls `applyConversions` with `includeRetired: true`, so the retired `page-kind-jsx-to-html` entry (`retiredFromLoadPath: true`, `retiredAfter: 17.7.0`) still rewrites a stored `kind: 'jsx'` page to `html` on the rehydration seam. That is the ADR-0087 addendum rule read in the shipped code; the server's call of that seam is objectstack's and outside this review's inputs.
- The console sample: `apps/console/src/sdui-jsx-preview.tsx` authors `kind: 'html'` at the head (objectui#12464 half 1).
- The types: `packages/types/src/layout.ts` declares `kind?: 'full' | 'slotted' | 'html' | 'react'`; the zod face extracts those four from the spec's own enum, which at next.2 is the identity. A `kind: 'jsx'` literal does not compile and does not parse.
- Writers in the tree: a PCRE grep of `packages/` and `apps/` source at the head for a `jsx` page kind finds only the retired-value pin in `packages/types/src/__tests__/page-kind-jsx-retired-12464.test.ts` and the new pin's own comments; the control `kind: 'html'` hits 55 files. The dev's measurement is reproduced.

**The `schema.kind` type read — sound.** `const kind = schema.kind` is `'full' | 'slotted' | 'html' | 'react' | undefined`; both comparisons (`'react'`, `'html'`) are members of the union, and a re-added `'jsx'` comparison is a TS2367, which is the compile-time guard the widening annotation on `main` existed to defeat. `Type Check` is green on the head.

**The narrowing is complete and nothing else narrows or widens.** The only behaviour change is the one arm. `layout.zod.ts` moves no code line: both hunks are comment text, and the re-attached-checks list now matches the dist (`checkPageSourceCompleteness` reads `html` and `react`; `checkPageRequiresKind` reads `COMPILED_PAGE_KINDS`, which is `html`). The app-shell server double reads the installed spec's `COMPILED_PAGE_KINDS` through `await vi.hoisted(async () => await import('@objectstack/spec/ui'))` instead of a hand copy of `html` and `jsx`; `@objectstack/spec` is a declared dependency of `@object-ui/app-shell` and `./ui` is an exported subpath, so the import resolves, and reading an installed dependency is not a cross-package source input. The `readonly unknown[]` view of the tuple is a test-local type widening so a stored `kind` of any value can be looked up; it reaches no shipped code.

**The pin.** `subject` is red while the arm exists (the compiled heading would paint), `same path` is red while the arm exists (the arm ignores `children`) and `control` is green in both worlds, so the file cannot pass on a renderer that compiles nothing. It renders through `ComponentRegistry.get('home', 'ui')`, which `page.tsx` registers to `PageRenderer`, and imports the renderers at module scope, not in a hook. The dev's ablation (arm restored, pin `2 failed | 1 passed`, components type-check red on TS2367, blob restored byte-equal) is consistent with that reading.

**Check-runs on the head.** Every required check is green: `Type Check`, `Test` and all 16 shards, `Test (dist pins)`, `Build & E2E`, `Lint`, `Repo Gates`, `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Claim Re-read`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Changeset Overwrite Report`, `Line Citation Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` (not governed), `Bundle Analysis`, `Build Docs`. `Live E2E (informational)` is red: judged from the run itself, the job failed at the step `Start ObjectStack backend (published packages)` about a minute in, every spec step after it (`Build console`, `Run live E2E allowlist`) was skipped, and the artefact step found no `backend.log`, which is the shape of the cold-cache npm install crash tracked as objectui#12649 that also hit `main`'s own PR #12648; this diff touches no `e2e/`, pin or backend file, and the lane is informational. The step log body itself was not retrievable through this session's proxy, so that judgment rests on the step roster, the duration and the missing artefact, not on the log text.

**Drift.** Between the merge-base `4be76e03` and `main` at review time (`efa9cb4f`) no touched path changed; the PR is mergeable.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/12486-drop-page-kind-jsx-arm.md`: `@object-ui/components: minor`, with the breaking semantics stated in the body and the migration spelled FROM `kind: 'jsx'` TO `kind: 'html'` with the one-line fix. That is this repo's version policy exactly: a breaking change in the fixed group is levelled `minor`, never `major` (`check-changeset-no-major` is the mechanical half, green on the head). The published surface the diff changes is one renderer behaviour in `@object-ui/components`; nothing in `@object-ui/types` changes behaviour (comments only) and the app-shell edit is a test. `Changeset Declaration` is green. The fixed group (40 packages, `components` and `types` included) versions together, so one entry is the right count.
- `.changeset/12464-retire-page-kind-jsx.md`: the pending entry's `Unchanged:` paragraph said the renderer still renders a stored `jsx` page as `html`. This PR makes that false in the same release, so deleting the paragraph (commit `240a30f9`) is the semver-face correction a reader of the shipped CHANGELOG needs; the head's second commit drops the now-redundant supersede sentence from the 12486 entry. Both edits are prose and change no level.
- `Clause-②: no` on the PR body and the claim is right: no published type, schema or export changes; the narrowing is of renderer behaviour, which is why the card owes this tier of review rather than the declaration tier. The line carries no `(narrowing)` arm; see ③.

- Out-of-scope finding, the 12464 changeset's `Unchanged:` paragraph: closed in this PR by commit `240a30f9`, authored under the adopting seat's session after the dev's report. The dev stopped at the surface boundary and reported, which is the right act. No gate reads that note's text (`scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs` consumes the ledger's kinds, not its notes), so it carries nothing here and is not a verdict input.
- Flag raised by this review, the `Clause-②:` spelling: the PR body's line is `Clause-②: no` with the narrowing declared in the section below it, and the claim carries the reason on a separate `Clause-② reason:` line. The record recogniser routes the narrowing face off the `(narrowing)` arm on that line (`--paths` refused to decide a face and asked for it), so as spelled a later reader classifies this PR's owed review as the declaration tier. This record serves the higher tier regardless, and the PR is not governed, so nothing mechanical is blocked; the one-word fix is to spell the PR body line `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, a prose surface for the lane seat. Not verdict-changing.
